policy_accepted: Historical observations may attach to an exact, source-backed sporely_taxon_id even when the concept is outside the currently supported macrofungi scope. Cache membership and scope state are tracked independently.

part_a.resolver_change: removed the 'concept present in pinned release' gate on Level 4 (canonical registry). When the registry has an anchor, resolve to that sporely_taxon_id regardless of release cache membership. Two new result fields: resolved_cache_state ('in_cache' | 'out_of_cache') and resolved_scope_state (release scope_state if in-cache, 'not_evaluated' otherwise). Contract §12 requirement.
part_a.result_model_change: ReconciliationResult now carries resolved_cache_state alongside resolved_scope_state. Cache membership and scope state are stored independently and never conflated.
part_a.web_sim_change: registry_concept table gained cache_state text not null default 'in_cache' check in ('in_cache','out_of_cache'). apply_reconciliation_manifest reads resolved_cache_state from the manifest and stores it verbatim.

cache_scope_independence_proof.note: in-cache concepts retain their real release scope_state (all 39 = 'include'); out-of-cache concepts carry 'not_evaluated' — the honest value when the macrofungi scope predicate did not evaluate them. No out-of-scope concept was rewritten to a generic scope value.

part_b.status: investigated; new immutable release build deferred to a focused session
part_b.observation_impact_projection: these 21 distinct identifiers cover ~21 observations (each id appeared once in the audit; no cross-observation reuse in the diagnostic).
part_b.root_cause: The 19 SQLite-present IDs are Norwegian non-fungi taxa (plants such as Cirsium arvense, Silene dioica, Berteroa incana, Stellaria nemorum, Rubus, ...). The current identity registry allocator (database/taxonomy/scripts/compile_release.py + identity_registry.py) allocates sporely_taxon_ids from a fungi-scoped W1 pipeline; non-fungi NorTaxa taxa are never seen by the allocator and therefore have no anchor. The 2 archive-only IDs are similarly out-of-scope entries that never entered the compiled SQLite. This is not a bug in the compiler — it is a scope decision at allocation time. Per the new W2E-A policy those historical observations must still receive stable identity; the proper repair widens the allocator's scope predicate to accept observation-derived non-fungi NorTaxa taxa.
part_b.why_deferred: Producing a new immutable release requires re-running compile_release.py (2114 lines) against the full COL XR + NorTaxa 1.284 source set, then the separate scope-exporter pass that produces global_macrofungi_tax-YYYY.MM.DD-NN. Both steps must be adjusted to include non-fungi observation-derived taxa without polluting the macrofungi search cache. Two structural changes are required: (1) compile_release.py — a new observation-derived-taxa input file, allocated as anchors under a separate audit trail; (2) the scope-exporter — emit their taxon_external_id.jsonl rows too. Each change requires targeted evidence, and the resulting new release must prove tax-2026.08.01-01 remains byte-identical while a sibling release tax-YYYY.MM.DD-NN carries the additional anchors. This is a multi-hour focused pipeline session with careful review; attempting it inline here would risk producing an ill-considered release.
part_b.safe_next_step_recommended: run W2E-A Part B as a scoped follow-up: add a new observation-derived-anchors input to compile_release.py that reads a curated JSONL of (source, namespace, external_id, taxonomicStatus=accepted) tuples from the desktop SQLite and NorTaxa 1.284 archive. Allocate anchors under the identity_registry allocator, re-shard the registry, then run the scope-exporter with the same macrofungi predicate. tax-2026.08.01-01 output must remain byte-identical when re-run; the new release carries a new manifest hash and a supplementary anchor-provenance artefact.
